title: Live Surveys
text: I build each survey with surveyframe and deploy it here as a self-contained static instrument. Responses are collected anonymously via Google Sheets. I declare the instrument object, analysis plan and structural model before data collection.

title: Live Surveys
text:
Open now

  AIC-RSAM Pilot Study
  
    
          Open now
        
    A pre-registered acceptance test of an AI-assisted conversational room-service booking system in Maldivian resorts. Participants complete a simulated booking prototype, then answer a post-use questionnaire covering six reflective constructs: Perceived AI Assistance, Perceived Order Assurance, Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Risk and Behavioural Intention to Use.
  
  
    Model: AIC-RSAM (PLS-SEM, 9 paths)
    Tool: surveyframe 0.4.2
    Conference: ICSRI 2026, Villa College
  
  
    Eligibility: Maldivian nationals or residents, aged 18 or above, who have stayed in a Maldivian resort within the past 12 months for at least 2 nights.
    Take the survey

title: Live Surveys
text:
About these surveys
All instruments on this page are built with the surveyframe R package and exported as single self-contained HTML files. Each file runs entirely in the browser with no server dependency. Responses are collected via a Google Apps Script endpoint and a local CSV download fires on every submission as a backup. The instrument definition, hypotheses and analysis plan are locked before data collection begins.

title: Open-Source Tools
text: Software for surveys, statistics, writing and reproducible research, selected for practical academic and teaching workflows. All are free and open-source.

title: Open-Source Tools
text:
Start here
If you are choosing quickly, start with JASP or jamovi for point-and-click statistics teaching, move to R + RStudio when you need programmable analysis and full reproducibility, use Quarto for reports and teaching materials, choose surveyframe when you need a full survey research pipeline from instrument design to analysis report inside R, and choose LimeSurvey or KoboToolbox when your data collection requires structured logic or offline fieldwork.

title: Open-Source Tools
text:
Statistics and analysis


  
    
      R + RStudio
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        R is the statistical language behind the teaching suite, and RStudio Desktop is the open-source development environment used for most of that work. Supports descriptive statistics, modelling, visualisation and reproducible reporting.
        Who should use it
        Researchers and postgraduate students who want full analytical control, reproducible outputs and a toolchain that scales from coursework to publishable analysis.
      
      
        Get R + RStudio
      
    
  

  
    
      JASP
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        A point-and-click statistics application developed by the University of Amsterdam. Covers standard frequentist tests and adds Bayesian counterparts alongside them. Output is formatted in APA style and exported directly to Word or PDF.
        Who should use it
        Undergraduate and postgraduate students, faculty who want a clean teaching tool and practitioners who need statistical results without writing code.
      
      
        Download JASP
      
    
  

  
    
      jamovi
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        Like JASP, jamovi provides a free, open-source interface for common statistical tests, with a spreadsheet-like data view. Supports mediation, moderation and factor analysis via the jmv and medmod modules, and runs R beneath the surface.
        Who should use it
        Students transitioning from Excel to proper statistical software, or anyone who needs a familiar spreadsheet layout alongside inferential statistics.
      
      
        Download jamovi
      
    
  

  
    
      PSPP
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        A free drop-in replacement for SPSS, maintained by the GNU project. Reads and writes .sav files, supports the most common SPSS syntax and covers regression, ANOVA, factor analysis and non-parametric tests.
        Who should use it
        Students and instructors who still work in SPSS-oriented environments but need a fully open-source option for teaching, practice or light applied analysis.
      
      
        Download PSPP

title: Open-Source Tools
text:
Survey and data collection


  
    
      surveyframe
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        An R package for end-to-end survey research workflows built around a typed instrument object. Visual instrument design, static HTML export, an embeddable Shiny module, response quality checking, psychometric diagnostics and reproducible HTML reporting. Live on CRAN.
        Who should use it
        Researchers and postgraduate students who design, deploy and analyse questionnaire-based studies in R and want a reproducible, self-contained pipeline from instrument design to analysis report.
      
      
        surveyframe on CRAN
      
    
  

  
    
      LimeSurvey
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        A full-featured open-source survey platform that supports complex branching logic, quota management, multiple languages and direct SPSS/R export. Can be self-hosted for data sovereignty or deployed through institutional hosting.
        Who should use it
        Researchers designing structured questionnaires with complex logic, multi-language instruments or any study requiring formal sampling controls.
      
      
        LimeSurvey.org
      
    
  

  
    
      KoboToolbox
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        Designed for data collection in low-connectivity environments. Supports offline collection on Android, GPS stamping, image capture and direct export to SPSS, Stata or Excel. Hosted free for academic researchers.
        Who should use it
        Researchers collecting field data in locations with unstable internet, distributed teams or device-based data capture requirements.
      
      
        KoboToolbox

title: Open-Source Tools
text:
Writing and publishing


  
    
      Quarto
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        The publishing system behind the statistics teaching suite. Produces the book, companion site, lecture decks, worked examples and related materials from a single source project, keeping content and output format separate.
        Who should use it
        Anyone producing textbooks, course materials, technical reports or academic papers who wants reproducible, version-controlled outputs.
      
      
        Get started with Quarto
      
    
  

  
    
      Zotero
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        Reference management software that captures references directly from browser pages, PDFs and DOI lookups. Generates citations and bibliographies in APA, MLA, Chicago and hundreds of journal-specific formats.
        Who should use it
        Students, researchers and faculty who manage literature reviews, academic writing or citation-heavy teaching materials.
      
      
        Download Zotero
      
    
  

  
    
      LibreOffice
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        A complete Microsoft Office alternative: Writer for documents, Calc for spreadsheets and Impress for presentations. Reads and writes .docx, .xlsx, and .pptx formats without conversion loss in most cases.
        Who should use it
        Students and instructors who want a fully open-source office suite for everyday writing, spreadsheets and slide preparation.
      
      
        Download LibreOffice

title: Open-Source Tools
text:
Reproducible research and teaching


  
    
      Git
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        The version-control system behind reproducible teaching and research workflows. Keeps manuscripts, slides, datasets and code in a traceable history and allows teaching materials to be rebuilt from known states.
        Who should use it
        Anyone maintaining textbooks, lecture materials, code or analysis scripts who wants version history, safer collaboration and repeatable release workflows.
      
      
        Download Git
      
    
  

  
    
      WebR
      
        
          Free & open-source
        
        WebR compiles R to WebAssembly, allowing R code to run directly in a web browser with no server, no installation and no account. Particularly effective for interactive statistical examples with live parameter changes.
        Who should use it
        Instructors and authors who want interactive browser-based statistical examples without requiring students to install software first.
      
      
        WebR documentation

title: About
text: I am a Senior Lecturer at the Qasim Ibrahim School of Business, Villa College, in Malé, Maldives, with a PhD in Management. I bring 24+ years of teaching, industry and administrative experience across South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean region, as a lecturer, researcher and consultant, always teaching in English to students for whom it is a second language. My aim is to raise the quality of business education and to make its methods usable by people without a statistics background.

title: About
text:
Research
My work sits where digital business, marketing analytics and maritime and blue economy research meet. Recurring methods are PLS-SEM, small-sample and exact inference, fuzzy DEMATEL, meta-analysis, bibliometrics and structural topic modelling.
Since 2014: 30+ publications; 24+ Scopus-indexed articles; 23+ conference presentations; 9+ funded projects. My Scopus h-index is 9+, with 6+ articles in Q1 journals and 12+ in Q2. I have led 3 of the funded projects, and 1 is active, on digital readiness and SME competitiveness in Oman’s blue economy sectors.
The research page lists everything, and the software page covers the R packages and browser tools that came out of it.

title: About
text:
Teaching
At Villa College I teach Marketing Management on the MBA and Customer Experience Management at Master’s level for senior managers in luxury resorts. At undergraduate level I teach Decision Making for Management, Digital Marketing, Project Management, 2 applied project modules under the University of the West of England partnership and an aviation internship. I supervise MBA dissertations as main supervisor, and I lead quality assurance for the School of Business, where I wrote and coordinated the SAQS accreditation the college now holds.
Before the Maldives I taught at Chiang Mai University’s College of Maritime Studies and Management in Thailand, at St Theresa International College and at institutions in India. I have run 21 workshops on R and open-source research software since 2017.

title: About
text:
Why this site exists
Most of what I publish is teaching material or research software that only earns its keep if people can get at it. So the textbooks are open access, the R packages are on CRAN under the MIT licence, and the templates and calculators run in a browser with nothing to install. The books, tools and teaching pages are the shortest routes in.

title: Books
text:
Decision Making for Management
A Student Textbook for Data-Informed Managerial Judgement. A Villa College course textbook teaching descriptive and inferential statistics through management decisions. Each chapter opens with a decision a manager faces, works from one teaching dataset of 200 customer records and runs every analysis in JASP or in PocketStat, a browser-based tool that needs no installation. Publishing on a rolling basis: the first two chapters are live now, covering data, measurement scales and descriptive statistics, and JASP and the normal distribution.

  Read the book →



  

Written for undergraduate business and management students meeting statistics for the first time, and for managers who need to judge the numbers they are handed before acting on them.

title: Books
text:
The Evidence-Based Digital Marketer
Digital Campaign Strategy, Open Marketing Analytics, and Responsible AI. A Villa College course textbook (MKTG3001) teaching digital marketing as an evidence-to-decision system: audience research, measurable objectives, persuasive content, channel strategy, measurement, automation and responsible AI use. Every chapter provides an open-source or free-access practice route. Publishing on a rolling basis: six of 15 weeks are live now, covering digital population research, classic-to-digital planning, persuasive imagery, messaging, display and YouTube, and search engine optimisation.

  Read the book →



  
    
  
   
  

Written for Villa College MKTG3001 students, and for any marketer or analyst who wants an evidence-first, open-practice route through digital marketing strategy rather than a platform-vendor playbook.
